problems.title: All hearts or all face cards
problems.statement: A player is dealt a hand of {{k}} cards from a standard 52-card deck. How many different hands consist entirely of hearts or entirely of face cards (or both)?

common_wrong.feedback: That counts hands of heart face cards twice: once as all hearts and once as all face cards. Subtract the overlap.
Multiplying counts hands formed by choosing {{k}} hearts and {{k}} face cards together. For an 'or' condition, add the counts and subtract the overlap.
That allows mixing hearts and face cards in the same hand. Every card in the hand must be of the same type: all hearts or all face cards.

solution.title: Hands of all hearts
solution.explanation: There are 13 hearts in the deck, so choosing {{k}} of them gives C(13,{{k}}) hands.

solution.title: Hands of all face cards
solution.explanation: There are 12 face cards (Jack, Queen, King in 4 suits), giving C(12,{{k}}) hands.

solution.title: Hands in the overlap
solution.explanation: Cards that are both hearts and face cards are the Jack, Queen, and King of hearts (3 cards), giving C(3,{{k}}) hands.

solution.title: Apply inclusion-exclusion
solution.explanation: Add the two counts and subtract the overlap that was counted twice.

problems.title: All red cards or all face cards
problems.statement: A player is dealt a hand of {{k}} cards from a standard 52-card deck. How many different hands consist entirely of red cards (hearts or diamonds) or entirely of face cards?

common_wrong.feedback: That counts hands of red face cards twice: once as red hands and once as face card hands.
There are 6 red face cards across hearts and diamonds, not just 3. Subtract hands drawn from all 6 red face cards.
That allows mixing red cards and non-red face cards within the same hand. The hand must be entirely red or entirely face cards.

solution.title: Hands of all red cards
solution.explanation: There are 26 red cards (13 hearts and 13 diamonds), giving C(26,{{k}}) hands.

solution.title: Hands of all face cards
solution.explanation: There are 12 face cards in the deck, giving C(12,{{k}}) hands.

solution.title: Hands in the overlap
solution.explanation: There are 6 red face cards (J, Q, K of hearts and diamonds), giving C(6,{{k}}) hands.

solution.title: Apply inclusion-exclusion
solution.explanation: Add the counts for red hands and face card hands, then subtract the red face card hands.

problems.title: All hearts or all face cards, but not both
problems.statement: A player is dealt a hand of {{k}} cards from a standard 52-card deck. How many different hands consist entirely of hearts or entirely of face cards, but not both?

common_wrong.feedback: Subtracting the overlap once leaves those hands counted once (inclusive OR). To remove hands with both properties completely, subtract the overlap twice.
That includes the hands satisfying both conditions twice instead of excluding them.

solution.title: Hands of all hearts and hands of all face cards
solution.explanation: There are C(13,{{k}}) hands of all hearts and C(12,{{k}}) hands of all face cards. Hands with both properties are counted twice.

solution.title: Hands in the overlap
solution.explanation: There are 3 heart face cards, giving C(3,{{k}}) hands that have both properties.

solution.title: Exclude the overlap completely
solution.explanation: Subtracting C(3,{{k}}) once reduces their count from 2 to 1; subtracting it again removes them entirely.
